question: Does reading the same allocator current/peak fields directly from nested statistics reduce observer cost at fixed admit2_32 workload?
hypothesis: Installed Torch memory_stats recursively flattens the full allocator dictionary for each public scalar query. Direct lookup may reduce observation cost without changing values; anomalous cProfile function times are not evidence of a cost magnitude or cause of earlier variation.
event: Same two-old-token prefix; incoming request actually submitted after four outputs each, cap2 delays its native admission and charges the full waiting time.
costs: Five original common warmups plus drained warmup per cell stay flat. Before capture verify installed Torch source SHA and flat/nested/flat field values without CUDA allocations, then set mode and restore flat in finally. Checks and artifact writes remain in parent/cycle accounting. Raw capture includes the full chosen observation path; no estimated-tax subtraction.
prestate: Source-ID normalized logical metadata including output tokens, positions, KV counts and pager slots/LRU. Physical KV IDs retained separately; no KV tensor equality claim.
scope: One existing OLMoE artificial-capacity triplet and fixed D policy; this tests instrumentation implementation cost, not a new scheduler contribution, production SLO, or general latency stability.
stops: GPU query failure/foreign processes, source mismatch, unstable or unequal pre-capture allocator fields, request/admission/accounting failure or failure to restore mode aborts and preserves attempt.
comparison: Within each adjacent pair nested versus flat plus both same-mode repeats; preserve all directions and all workload/route/cache/output differences. First damaged CPU-profile campaign remains separate.
continuation: If same fields and work are preserved and observer cost falls, adopt nested reading as the common measurement path before returning to continuous arrivals. Otherwise retain flat and report no established advantage. Neither outcome proves the cause of prior drift.
ordering: Four same-policy episodes: flat,nested,nested,flat. ABBA diagnostic, two observations per implementation, no statistical noise bound.
action: Only three expert _apply allocator reads switch flat public scalar queries versus nested dictionary lookup. Same locations, query count, current/peak fields. Both arms share the helper overhead; no Torch global patch, policy change or cProfile.
required_costs: all original timing and resource fields
